region: Lodi · Seneca Lake, Finger Lakes, New York
about: Lamoreaux Landing sits on the eastern shore of Seneca Lake, on a farm the Wagner family has worked for generations. Mark Wagner, a second-generation grape grower, took over the family farm in 1978, planted vinifera vines, and founded the winery in 1990. Today it is run with his nephew Josh Wig, a retired Navy officer and fourth-generation farmer, and head winemaker Jesse Alexander. Every wine is made and bottled on site, and only from grapes the family grows itself.

The estate has more than 130 acres of vines divided into over 50 blocks, mostly on Honeoye silt loam and Lansing gravelly loam, with the deep lake moderating the cold. The vines are trained on a Scott-Henry trellis, and the farm is certified under New York’s Sustainable Winegrowing Program, with solar panels supplying about 90 percent of the winery’s power. Block 137 is a single-block Merlot, bottled on its own rather than blended into the estate reds.

Merlot is a challenge this far north, and the winery’s version leans toward freshness rather than weight. Wine Spectator has described earlier vintages as light-bodied and fresh, with cherry fruit and a hint of vanilla. The 2021 is warm and spicy on the nose, with cedar, cinnamon, plum and cherry, supple tannins and an earthy freshness.
